condition_other: overactive bladder (acetic acid-induced) in a subset of experiments
readout_other: intra-bladder pressure (micturition interval); H&E of tibial nerve (supplement)
direction_notes: 100 Hz PRF produced the most potent micturition inhibition (normalized interval 1.720), 10 Hz and 1 kHz gave little or no effect; the effect was abolished by sciatic nerve block and persisted in an OAB model and in a freely moving rat.
safety_notes: H&E staining of the stimulated tibial nerve showed no detectable morphological changes compared with the contralateral nerve; hydrophone-measured peak pressure and MI were stated to be below safety thresholds (Fig. S2).

exposures.label: LIFU-TNS at PRF 10 Hz, 100 Hz, 1 kHz

timing.protocol_description: Stimulation was applied continuously for 30 minutes, followed by a 1 hour resting period; PRF conditions (10 Hz, 100 Hz, 1 kHz) were applied as sequential trials in each subject in a designed order (Table S1).

source_quotes.n_subjects: Comprehensive result for all 6 rats can be found in Fig. S3.

source_quotes.exposures[0].device.manufacturer: 2) LIFU Stimulation System Configuration: For US stimulation, a focused type single transducer (V301, Olympus, USA) was used for LIFU generation.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: To investigate the PRF-dependent effects of LIFU-TNS, PRF values of 10 Hz, 100 Hz, and 1 kHz were selected. These values were chosen to align with the frequency domains of electrostimulation-based TNS, in which low-frequency stimulation (10–20 Hz) is associated with micturition inhibition, while higher frequencies (50-100 Hz, > 1 kHz; not typically applied for OAB treatment) have been reported to elicit excitatory responses.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: Stimulation was applied continuously for 30 minutes, followed by a 1 hour resting period to minimize potential residual effects.
